status: pre-registered before any extraction with these descriptions
delta_vs_main: exactly one description changes: seller_vat_id (EIN-inclusive). The other nine are byte-identical to invoiceloop/ingest.py::FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS at the pre-registration commit
rejected_alternative: BROADCAST_ADK_DRAFT_2026-08-10.json made seller_vat_id EIN-exclusive ('excluding EIN, FCC ID, or station callsign'). Rejected: DocILE vendor_tax_id is 85% EIN (648/760 NN-NNNNNNN format, 3 VAT-style), so excluding EIN tells the extractor to skip the value truth annotates, manufacturing artificial absence slots. The pilot's silent_wrong drop under that draft partly came from not extracting at all — not extracting cannot err, but it also cannot hit

descriptions.due_date: Explicitly printed calendar date labelled as the payment due date. Do not put a date calculated from Net or other payment terms here; the deterministic post-extraction field calculated_due_date is separate.
descriptions.seller_name: Full legal name of the seller.
descriptions.seller_vat_id: Seller US federal tax ID (EIN / Federal ID), or VAT identifier where present.
descriptions.buyer_name: Full legal name of the buyer.
descriptions.amount_due: Amount the buyer must actually pay.

evaluation.sample: deterministic _sample_doc_ids (schema-eval-v1 hash order) over the workspace's 300 dev docs; baseline arm = the stored understand responses of run-0002
evaluation.moving_parts: TWO, not one: the workspace's stored schema predates the 3c0568f merge, so the baseline responses carry the old due_date text ('Payment due date.') as well as the old seller_vat_id text. The eval therefore measures the combined (due_date narrowing + EIN-inclusive seller_vat_id) delta against the stored baseline. The due_date narrowing is already pilot-validated (BROADCAST_PILOT_RESULT_2026-08-10.json: silent_wrong 23 -> 17 under a draft that included it); the marginal isolation of seller_vat_id alone would need a fresh 30-call baseline and was judged not worth the spend

predictions.seller_vat_id_value_hits: up — the EIN-inclusive text lets the extractor keep EINs it previously dropped or misfiled
predictions.review_load: not up (Gate 3); the pilot's EIN-exclusive draft raised review slots 191 -> 201, and that direction is part of why it was rejected
predictions.note: predictions exist to make deviation visible; deviation is recorded, not a voiding condition

promotion_rule: gate_verdict on the reextract eval + human signature; silent_wrong improvement is NOT the promotion criterion (design doc step 2: the schema layer's job is preventing wrong-field mapping, not cutting the queue)
